title: Right resolution in a subcategory (Stacks 05T6, part (1))
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal I \subset \Ob(\mathcal A)$ be a subset containing $0$ such that every object of $\mathcal A$ is a subobject of an element of $\mathcal I$. Let $a \in \mathbf Z$. Given a cochain complex $K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $K^n=0$ for $n<a$, there exist a cochain complex $I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal A$ and a quasi-isomorphism $K^\bullet \to I^\bullet$ (a morphism of complexes inducing isomorphisms $H^n(K^\bullet)\to H^n(I^\bullet)$ for all $n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]) with $K^n \to I^n$ injective and $I^n \in \mathcal I$ for all $n$ and $I^n=0$ for $n<a$.

proof.text: Notation: for a cochain complex $X^\bullet$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $\pi_X^n:X^n\to C_X^n:=\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})$ be the cokernel and $\bar d_X^n:C_X^n\to X^{n+1}$ the morphism with $\bar d_X^n\pi_X^n=d_X^n$. **Step 1 (induction hypothesis; dual of $IH_n$ in 05T7).** For an integer $n\ge a-1$ let $IH_n$ be the statement: there are objects $I^j\in\mathcal I$ for $j\le n$ with $I^j=0$ for $j<a$, morphisms $d^j:I^j\to I^{j+1}$ for $j\le n-1$, and monomorphisms $\alpha^j:K^j\to I^j$ for $j\le n$, such that (i) $d^j\alpha^j=\alpha^{j+1}d_K^j$ for $j\le n-1$; (ii) $d^{j+1}d^j=0$ for $j\le n-2$; (iii) for $j\le n-1$ the morphism $\operatorname{Ker}(d_K^j)/\operatorname{Im}(d_K^{j-1})\to\operatorname{Ker}(d^j)/\operatorname{Im}(d^{j-1})$ induced by $\alpha^j$ is an isomorphism; (iv) the morphism $\bar\alpha^n:C_K^n=\operatorname{Coker}(d_K^{n-1})\to C_I^n=\operatorname{Coker}(d^{n-1})$ induced by $\alpha^n$ (it exists by (i) for $j=n-1$) is a monomorphism. $IH_{a-1}$ holds: take $I^j=0$ for $j\le a-1$ (allowed since $0\in\mathcal I$), all $d^j$ and $\alpha^j$ zero; each $\alpha^j:K^j=0\to0$ is a monomorphism, (i)-(iii) hold since all objects in degrees $\le a-1$ are $0$, and (iv) holds since $C_K^{a-1}$ is a quotient of $K^{a-1}=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387), part (1); its proof is "dual to Lemma Tag 05T7" (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, line 5302), whose proof of part (1): the induction hypothesis $IH_n$ and the remark that $IH_{a+1}$ holds with $P^j=0$, dualized

proof.text: **Step 2 (construction in degree $n+1$).** Assume $IH_n$. Since $d_K^nd_K^{n-1}=0$ there is $\bar d_K^n:C_K^n\to K^{n+1}$ with $\bar d_K^n\pi_K^n=d_K^n$, and $\bar\alpha^n:C_K^n\to C_I^n$ is a monomorphism by (iv). Let $(P,u,v)$ be a pushout of $\bar d_K^n$ and $\bar\alpha^n$, i.e. $P=K^{n+1}\amalg_{C_K^n}C_I^n$ with $u:K^{n+1}\to P$, $v:C_I^n\to P$, $u\bar d_K^n=v\bar\alpha^n$ (pushouts exist in $\mathcal A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel](d); this is the dual of the fibre product $K^{n-1}\times_{K^n}\operatorname{Ker}(d^n)$ of 05T7). By hypothesis on $\mathcal I$ choose a monomorphism $i:P\to I^{n+1}$ with $I^{n+1}\in\mathcal I$ (note $n+1\ge a$, so no vanishing is required). Put $\alpha^{n+1}=i\circ u:K^{n+1}\to I^{n+1}$ and $d^n=i\circ v\circ\pi_I^n:I^n\to I^{n+1}$. Since $\bar\alpha^n$ is a monomorphism, $u$ is a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono] (with $a=\bar\alpha^n$, $b=\bar d_K^n$, $a'=u$), so $\alpha^{n+1}$ is a monomorphism as a composite of monomorphisms.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387), part (1); its proof is "dual to Lemma Tag 05T7" (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, line 5302), whose proof of part (1): the choice of a surjection $P^{n-1}\to K^{n-1}\times_{K^n}\Ker(d^n)$, dualized to an injection of the pushout $K^{n+1}\amalg_{C_K^n}C_I^n$ into an element of $\mathcal I$

proof.text: **Step 3 (conditions (i) and (ii) in degree $n$).** $d^n\alpha^n=iv\pi_I^n\alpha^n=iv\bar\alpha^n\pi_K^n=iu\bar d_K^n\pi_K^n=iu\,d_K^n=\alpha^{n+1}d_K^n$, using $\bar\alpha^n\pi_K^n=\pi_I^n\alpha^n$ (definition of $\bar\alpha^n$) and the pushout square. And $d^nd^{n-1}=iv\,\pi_I^nd^{n-1}=0$ since $\pi_I^n$ is a cokernel of $d^{n-1}$. With $IH_n$ this gives (i) for $j\le n$ and (ii) for $j\le n-1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387), part (1); its proof is "dual to Lemma Tag 05T7" (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, line 5302), whose proof of part (1): "the reader easily checks that $IH_{n-1}$ holds", dualized; this step and Steps 4-5 write that check out

proof.text: **Step 4 (condition (iii) in degree $n$).** Since $\pi_I^n$ is an epimorphism and $d^n=(iv)\pi_I^n$, the morphism $\bar d_I^n:C_I^n\to I^{n+1}$ is $iv$, and $\operatorname{Ker}(iv)=\operatorname{Ker}(v)$ as subobjects of $C_I^n$ because $i$ is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-kernel-on-cokernel], $H^n(K)\cong\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_K^n)$ and $H^n(I)\cong\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_I^n)=\operatorname{Ker}(v)$ (here $H^n(I)$ only involves $d^{n-1},d^n$, already defined), and the map $H^n(K)\to H^n(I)$ induced by $\alpha^n$ is an isomorphism if and only if the morphism $\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_K^n)\to\operatorname{Ker}(v)$ induced by $\bar\alpha^n$ is. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-kernel-iso] to the pushout square with $w=C_K^n$, $f=\bar d_K^n$, $g=\bar\alpha^n$ (a monomorphism), $h=u$, $k=v$: the morphism $\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_K^n)\to\operatorname{Ker}(v)$ induced by $\bar\alpha^n$ is an isomorphism. Hence (iii) holds for $j=n$, and with $IH_n$ for all $j\le n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387), part (1); its proof is "dual to Lemma Tag 05T7" (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, line 5302), whose proof of part (1): the isomorphisms $\Ker(d^j)/\Im(d^{j-1})\to H^j(K^\bullet)$ in $IH_{n-1}$, dualized

proof.text: **Step 5 (condition (iv) in degree $n+1$).** As $\pi_K^n$ and $\pi_I^n$ are epimorphisms, a morphism kills $d_K^n=\bar d_K^n\pi_K^n$ iff it kills $\bar d_K^n$, and kills $d^n=(iv)\pi_I^n$ iff it kills $iv$; so $C_K^{n+1}=\operatorname{Coker}(\bar d_K^n)$ and $C_I^{n+1}=\operatorname{Coker}(iv)$, and $\bar\alpha^{n+1}$ is the morphism $\operatorname{Coker}(\bar d_K^n)\to\operatorname{Coker}(iv)$ induced by $\alpha^{n+1}=iu$. It factors as $\operatorname{Coker}(\bar d_K^n)\xrightarrow{\theta}\operatorname{Coker}(v)\xrightarrow{\bar\imath}\operatorname{Coker}(iv)$, with $\theta$ induced by $u$ and $\bar\imath$ induced by $i$ (both composites agree after precomposing with the epimorphism $K^{n+1}\to\operatorname{Coker}(\bar d_K^n)$). $\theta$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-cokernel-iso] applied to the same pushout square ($f=\bar d_K^n$, $g=\bar\alpha^n$, $h=u$, $k=v$), and $\bar\imath$ is a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-cokernel-map-mono-of-mono] ($i$ is a monomorphism). Hence $\bar\alpha^{n+1}$ is a monomorphism. Together with Steps 2-4, $IH_{n+1}$ holds, the data of $IH_n$ being kept unchanged.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387), part (1); its proof is "dual to Lemma Tag 05T7" (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, line 5302), whose proof of part (1): the condition that $\alpha:\Ker(d^n)\to\Ker(d_K^n)$ is surjective in $IH_{n-1}$, dualized

proof.text: **Step 6 (conclusion).** Starting from $IH_{a-1}$ (Step 1) and applying Steps 2-5 recursively (choosing at each stage $n$ the pushout and the monomorphism $i$), each $IH_{n+1}$ extends the data of $IH_n$ without changing it, so we obtain objects $I^n\in\mathcal I$ for all $n$ with $I^n=0$ for $n<a$, morphisms $d^n:I^n\to I^{n+1}$ and monomorphisms $\alpha^n:K^n\to I^n$ for all $n$. By (ii) of every $IH_m$, $d^{n+1}d^n=0$ for all $n$, so $I^\bullet$ is a cochain complex; by (i), $\alpha=(\alpha^n)$ is a morphism of complexes $K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; and by (iii) of $IH_{n+1}$, $H^n(\alpha):H^n(K^\bullet)\to H^n(I^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$ (for $n<a$ both sides are $0$). Thus $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism with every $\alpha^n$ injective, $I^n\in\mathcal I$ for all $n$, and $I^n=0$ for $n<a$.

split_report.summary: Stacks 05T6 is proved there only as 'dual to 05T7'; the proof dualizes the inductive construction of 05T7(1): induction hypothesis IH_n (degrees <= n built, alpha mono, cohomology iso below n, induced map on Coker(d^{n-1}) mono), base IH_{a-1} using 0 in I, step via the pushout K^{n+1} amalg_{Coker d_K^{n-1}} Coker(d_I^{n-1}) embedded into an element of I. The check that 05T7 leaves to the reader is written out with three new Mathlib leaves (kernels and cokernels across a pushout along a mono, cokernel map induced by a mono, cohomology as kernel on the cokernel) and existing leaves lem-weil-pbc-pushout-cokernel-iso, lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono, lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel. Statement unchanged in content; def-weil-abstract-derived-category cited for cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms and I^bullet introduced explicitly. Mathlib has only the injective case (CM5a exists_mono_quasiIso_injective, with bound a-1), not the general class.

reviewed.note: 6 steps dualizing Stacks 05T7 (05T6 is 'dual' in Stacks): induction hypothesis with the cokernel map C_K^n -> C_I^n a monomorphism; pushout of C_K^n -> K^{n+1} along it, embedded into an element of I; (i), (ii); H^n via kernels on cokernels and the pushout-kernel isomorphism (g mono); (iv) in the next degree via the pushout-cokernel isomorphism and mono of cokernel maps along a mono; recursion. 3 new composed Mathlib leaves (CommSq.lean 151, 137; ShortComplex/HomologicalComplex.lean 321; verified by L). Statement: definitions cited, I^bullet introduced.

lean.statement: theorem exists_mono_quasiIso_in_subcategory (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (𝓘 : Set C) (hzero : (0 : C) ∈ 𝓘) (hembed : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y), Y ∈ 𝓘 ∧ Mono f) (a : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a → IsZero (K.X n)) : ∃ (I : CochainComplex C ℤ) (α : K ⟶ I), QuasiIso α ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Mono (α.f n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, I.X n ∈ 𝓘) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n < a → IsZero (I.X n))
